ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two intersecting circles in the figure; the circle on the left is larger, and the circle on the right is smaller. They have two intersection points, one above and one below, and the labeled P is the upper intersection point. A straight line passes through P, intersects the larger circle on the left at Q toward the upper left, and intersects the smaller circle on the right at R toward the lower right, so QP and PR are in opposite directions on the same straight line. The problem statement gives that the radii of the two circles are respectively 8 and 6, the distance between the centers is 12, and QP = PR. Reasoning: Let the center of the left circle with radius 8 be O1, and the center of the right circle with radius 6 be O2. Let a = P - O1 and b = P - O2, then |a| = 8, |b| = 6, and |a - b| = O1O2 = 12. Let the unit vector pointing from P to R be u, and let x = QP = PR. Since Q = P - xu is on the left circle and R = P + xu is on the right circle, expanding the circle equations: |a - xu|^2 = |a|^2 gives x = 2u·a; |b + xu|^2 = |b|^2 gives x = -2u·b. Therefore u·(a + b) = 0, that is, u is perpendicular to a + b. From |a - b|^2 = 12^2, there is 8^2 + 6^2 - 2a·b = 144, so a·b = -22. Thus |a + b|^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 + 2a·b = 64 + 36 - 44 = 56, and a·(a + b) = |a|^2 + a·b = 64 - 22 = 42. Since u is a unit direction perpendicular to a + b, the square of u·a equals the square of the projection of a in the direction perpendicular to a + b: |a|^2 - (a·(a+b))^2 / |a+b|^2 = 64 - 42^2/56 = 64 - 31.5 = 32.5. Therefore x^2 = 4(u·a)^2 = 4 · 32.5 = 130.

method.method_draft: First read the figure as two intersecting circles, with P the upper intersection and a straight line through P meeting the larger left circle again at Q and the smaller right circle again at R; QP and PR lie on opposite rays of the same line. Let the centers be O1 and O2, with radii 8 and 6 respectively, and O1O2 = 12. Put vectors a = P - O1 and b = P - O2, so |a| = 8, |b| = 6, and |a - b| = 12. Let u be the unit vector from P toward R and let x = QP = PR. Because Q = P - xu lies on the first circle and R = P + xu lies on the second circle, expanding the two circle equations gives x = 2u·a and x = -2u·b. Hence u·(a + b) = 0, so u is perpendicular to a + b. Use the law of cosines in triangle O1PO2 to get a·b = (8^2 + 6^2 - 12^2)/2 = -22. Then |a + b|^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 + 2a·b = 56 and a·(a + b) = 8^2 + a·b = 42. Since u is the unit direction perpendicular to a + b, compute x^2 = 4 times the squared projection of a onto that perpendicular direction: x^2 = 4( |a|^2 - (a·(a+b))^2/|a+b|^2 ) = 4(64 - 42^2/56) = 130.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a common secant line through P: it cuts the left circle at Q and P, and the right circle at P and R, with QP = PR. Let x = QP = PR. Put the drawn line QR as a horizontal axis with P at 0, Q at -x, and R at x. The midpoint of chord QP is then at -x/2, and the midpoint of chord PR is at x/2. By the perpendicular-from-center-to-chord theorem, the center of the left circle lies on the perpendicular through -x/2, and the center of the right circle lies on the perpendicular through x/2. From the image, both centers lie on the same side of the secant line, so if their perpendicular distances from the line are h1 and h2, then h1^2 + (x/2)^2 = 8^2 and h2^2 + (x/2)^2 = 6^2. Their horizontal separation is x and their vertical separation is |h1 - h2|, while their actual distance is 12. Therefore x^2 + (h1 - h2)^2 = 12^2. Substitute h1 = sqrt(64 - x^2/4) and h2 = sqrt(36 - x^2/4). With s = x^2, solve s + (sqrt(64 - s/4) - sqrt(36 - s/4))^2 = 144. Expanding and squaring gives 4(64 - s/4)(36 - s/4) = (s/2 - 44)^2, which simplifies to s = 130.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有两个相交的圆，左边的圆较大，右边的圆较小。点 P 是两个圆的一个交点。一条斜直线经过 Q、P、R，其中 Q 和 P 是左圆上的 chord endpoints，P 和 R 是右圆上的 chord endpoints。图中 QP 与 PR 在同一直线上，且题设给出 QP = PR。两个圆心虽然没有画出，但从图形位置看，它们都在这条斜直线的同一侧。

再推理：设 QP = PR = x。把直线 QPR 作为水平轴，并令 P 的坐标为 0，则 Q 在 -x，R 在 x。左圆中弦 QP 的中点在 -x/2，右圆中弦 PR 的中点在 x/2。圆心到弦的垂线经过弦的中点，所以左圆圆心的水平坐标为 -x/2，右圆圆心的水平坐标为 x/2。因此两个圆心的水平距离为 x。

左圆半径为 8，右圆半径为 6。设左圆圆心到直线的垂直距离为 h1，右圆圆心到直线的垂直距离为 h2。由半径、半弦长、垂距构成直角三角形：
h1^2 + (x/2)^2 = 8^2 = 64，
h2^2 + (x/2)^2 = 6^2 = 36。
所以 h1 = sqrt(64 - x^2/4)，h2 = sqrt(36 - x^2/4)。

因为两个圆心在直线同一侧，所以圆心之间的垂直距离为 |h1 - h2|。题设圆心距为 12，因此
x^2 + (h1 - h2)^2 = 12^2 = 144。
令 s = x^2，代入得
s + (sqrt(64 - s/4) - sqrt(36 - s/4))^2 = 144。
展开：
s + 64 - s/4 + 36 - s/4 - 2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = 144，
100 + s/2 - 2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = 144。
所以
2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = s/2 - 44。
两边平方：
4(64 - s/4)(36 - s/4) = (s/2 - 44)^2。
展开化简：
9216 - 100s + s^2/4 = s^2/4 - 44s + 1936，
7280 = 56s，
s = 130。
因此 QP^2 = 130。

s + (sqrt(64 - s/4) - sqrt(36 - s/4))^2 = 144。
展开：
s + 64 - s/4 + 36 - s/4 - 2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = 144，
100 + s/2 - 2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = 144。
所以
2sqrt((64 - s/4)(36 - s/4)) = s/2 - 44。
两边平方：
4(64 - s/4)(36 - s/4) = (s/2 - 44)^2。
展开化简：
9216 - 100s + s^2/4 = s^2/4 - 44s + 1936，
7280 = 56s，
s = 130。
因此 QP^2 = 130。

raw_record.original_question: In the adjoining figure, two circles of radii 6 and 8 are drawn with their centers 12 units apart. At $P$, one of the points of intersection, a line is drawn in such a way that the chords $QP$ and $PR$ have equal length. Find the square of the length of $QP$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: There are two intersecting circles in the figure; the circle on the left is larger, and the circle on the right is smaller. They have two intersection points, one above and one below, and the labeled P is the upper intersection point. A straight line passes through P, intersects the larger circle on the left at Q toward the upper left, and intersects the smaller circle on the right at R toward the lower right, so QP and PR are in opposite directions on the same straight line. The problem statement gives that the radii of the two circles are respectively 8 and 6, the distance between the centers is 12, and QP = PR.

Reasoning: Let the center of the left circle with radius 8 be O1, and the center of the right circle with radius 6 be O2. Let a = P - O1 and b = P - O2, then |a| = 8, |b| = 6, and |a - b| = O1O2 = 12. Let the unit vector pointing from P to R be u, and let x = QP = PR. Since Q = P - xu is on the left circle and R = P + xu is on the right circle, expanding the circle equations: |a - xu|^2 = |a|^2 gives x = 2u·a; |b + xu|^2 = |b|^2 gives x = -2u·b. Therefore u·(a + b) = 0, that is, u is perpendicular to a + b.

From |a - b|^2 = 12^2, there is 8^2 + 6^2 - 2a·b = 144, so a·b = -22. Thus |a + b|^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 + 2a·b = 64 + 36 - 44 = 56, and a·(a + b) = |a|^2 + a·b = 64 - 22 = 42. Since u is a unit direction perpendicular to a + b, the square of u·a equals the square of the projection of a in the direction perpendicular to a + b: |a|^2 - (a·(a+b))^2 / |a+b|^2 = 64 - 42^2/56 = 64 - 31.5 = 32.5. Therefore x^2 = 4(u·a)^2 = 4 · 32.5 = 130.
